title: Spring Swans
text:
swans also die in spring

and there it floated

dead on a Sunday

turning sideways

in the current

and I went to the traffic circle

and made out

gods in cars,

dogs, women

turning,

and death

rushed down my throat

like a mouse,

and I heard the people coming

with their picnic baskets

and their laughter

and I felt guilty

for the swan

as if death

were something shameful

and I went away

like an idiot

and left them

my beautiful swan.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the dead swan, public laughter, and the speaker's shame before ordinary death.

title: Creative Act
text:
For the broken egg on the floor

for the 5th of July

for the fish in the fishbowl

for the old man in room No. 9

for the cat on the wall.


For yourself

not for fame

or for money

you have to keep fighting.


When you get old

the attraction diminishes

it is easier when one is young

anyone can reach

the heights now and then.


The key consists in

enduring.


Anything that helps

so that

this life keeps dancing

in front of

Lady Death.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's motive for making art as endurance before Lady Death.

title: The History of Melancholy...
text:
the history of melancholy

includes us all.

I twist among the dirty sheets

while I fix my gaze

on the blue walls

and nothing.

I have grown so used to melancholy

that

I greet it like an old

friend.

now I will have 15 minutes of affliction

for the redhead who left,

I will tell the gods.

I feel really bad

really sad

then I get up

PURIFIED

though I have solved

nothing

(...)

there is something wrong with me

besides

melancholy
editorial_note: The translation preserves the casual ritual of melancholy, brief purification, and unresolved final admission.

title: The Laughing Heart
text:
your life is your life

do not let it be beaten into damp submission

stay alert

there are exits


there is a light somewhere

it may not be much light but

it beats the darkness


stay alert

the gods will offer you chances

know them

take them


you cannot beat death but

you can beat death in life, sometimes

and the more often you learn to do it

the more light there will be


your life is your life

know it while you have it


you are marvelous

the gods wait to delight

in you.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the direct exhortation and the recurring light against submission and death.

title: Confession
text:
waiting for death

like a cat

that will jump onto the

bed.


I am sorry for

my wife.

She will see this

body

stiff

and white.


She will shake it once, then

perhaps again:

"Hank"

Hank will not

answer.


It is not my death that

worries me, it is my wife

alone with this

pile of nothing.


I want her to know

that every night

sleeping beside her.

Even the useless

arguments

were splendid

things.


And the hard

words

I was always afraid to

say

can now be

said:


"I love you"
editorial_note: The translation keeps the deathbed tenderness and the final words withheld until after death.
